name: Week 31 Optional KB — Dead Cluster Flow
description:
**Optional and deliberately short.** Run it whenever a window opens after the gym work; it is not tied to a weekday and missing it does not make the week incomplete.

**The Dead Cluster Flow returns — seven beats, one bell, one side at a time.** A dead cluster is a clean off the floor into a front squat into a press overhead, with the bell set back down dead between reps. From there the chain runs through a snatch, a straight-arm lateral hold, a swing that arcs out around the hip, a clean back to the rack, a reverse lunge and a squat with the bell racked on one side only.

**It is overhead-heavy, and a new crackle showed up in the left shoulder last week.** Go light, and treat the lateral hold as the first thing to drop.

dayOverview.theme: One long flow carries the whole day, with the left-arm curl dose after it. Short on purpose — the three gym days are the week, and this is whatever is left over. Rounds are the variable, never the bell.

spotlights.why: The opening beat and the one that sets the tone: the bell starts dead on the floor every rep, so there is no momentum to borrow. Legs clean it, legs squat it, legs start the press — if the arm is doing the work, the bell is too heavy.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W32 — kickstand complex or the overhead mobility complex returns. W33 — outside snatch flow comes back around.
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: the dead cluster press, the snatch, the lateral hold, both cleans. This is the most overhead work in the week.
🔥 near-failure last set OK: KB curl — **except this week**, see below.

**⚠️ THE LEFT SHOULDER IS NEW AND THE RIGHT ONE HAS A HISTORY. GO LIGHT — 20-25.** Three of the seven beats put the bell overhead or on a long lever. **Pack the shoulder DOWN on every lockout, and drop the straight-arm lateral hold first** if either side complains. Bailing on a beat is the correct move, not a failed round.
**Rounds are the variable, not the bell.** Two rounds per side is the prescription. A third only if it genuinely feels strong.
**The bell goes dead on the floor between cluster reps.** That is the point of the name — no bouncing one rep off the last.
**KB curl: left arm first, stop short of straight, no near-failure this week.** The left bicep tendon is still irritable and the bell loads the bottom hard.
**Banded shoulder prep + protective shrug stay in the warm-up**, even on the twenty-minute version — and on this of all days.

sets.name: Warm-Up — Halos + Bottoms-Up Cuff Prep + Cossacks
sets.notes: Light bell throughout. The bottoms-up work matters more than usual today — it is cuff prep, and the flow is about to ask for a lot of overhead lockouts.

exercises.notes: Slow, close to the head. Shoulders packed down. **Take the left side slower.**

Light bell inverted. Cuff prep and grip — and it rehearses the packed-down lockout that everything else today is about to ask for. **If the left will not hold the bell quiet and stacked, that is your signal to go lighter for the whole session.**
**Your readiness screen.** Deep as the hips allow, heel down. Read it against your own normal.
Hinged slightly forward, tight fists, thumbs tucked.
Protective activation. Down and back at the top.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~2 min)
sets.notes:
One round of all seven, about two minutes. Sustained tension, no rest between positions. **This is the KB-day shoulder anchor and it does not come out** — and today is the day it earns its place.

**Tired-day version:** 6 reps each. Exhausted: do it anyway at whatever range is smooth.

exercises.notes: Arms overhead, pull apart without letting the ribs flare.
Slow and controlled. Blades down and together.
Thumbs up, arms to a T. Traps stay quiet.
Rear delts. Lead with the elbows.
Hold the V overhead. Ribs down, shoulders packed.

sets.name: 🌀 Dead Cluster Flow — Seven Beats, One Side at a Time
sets.notes:
**LIGHT bell — 20-25. Two rounds per side**, ~60s between rounds. Run the whole chain on one side, then the other.

🔆 **The opening beat sets the tone.** A dead cluster is a clean off the floor → front squat → press overhead, and **the bell goes back down dead on the floor between reps.** There is no momentum carried from one rep to the next, which is the whole reason it is called dead — the legs have to start every single one.

**The other six, in plain words:**
- **Snatch** — here it runs overhead-to-overhead out of the cluster's lockout, not up from the floor
- **Straight-arm lateral hold** — the bell raised out to the side to shoulder height on a straight arm, held briefly. **This is the first thing to drop today**
- **Outside pendulum swing** — two single-arm swings that arc out around the working hip rather than between the legs; brace so the torso does not twist toward the bell
- **Tactical clean** — threaded back into the rack out of the second swing, no reset and no yank
- **Reverse lunge** — bell stays racked, step back, both knees to about 90°, drive through the front heel
- **Offset rack squat** — bell racked on one side only; the job is resisting the pull toward the loaded side

🛑 **The shoulder rules:** light bell, **pack it DOWN on every lockout**, ribs down. **If either shoulder talks, drop the lateral hold and keep going** — the flow survives losing a beat. Bailing is the designed exit, not a failed round.

sets.name: Left-Arm Curl Dose 🛑
sets.notes: One round, and the only loaded arm work here. This stays because the left arm wants **frequency**, not intensity.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD: light bell, ~25-35. LEFT ARM FIRST — match the right to it.**
- **Upper arm pinned to the ribs**, elbow does not drift forward
- **Stop short of a fully straight arm at the bottom** — the bell loads that end position harder than a dumbbell does, and that end position is what the left tendon dislikes
- Shoulder packed down, no shrug to start

**No near-failure this week.** Calm load, full control.

sets.name: Cooldown (Shoulder + Hip + QL Release)
sets.notes:
Overhead-heavy day — the shoulders come first for once.

**Tired-day version:** 30s each.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm, elbow at MID height. Earned today.
Passive. Let the shoulders decompress after all that lockout work.
Adductors — the lunges and lateral work earned this.
30s each side. Let the QL downshift after the hinge work.

tips: Rounds are the variable, never the bell. Light — 20-25.
The bell goes dead on the floor between cluster reps. No bouncing one rep off the last.
Drop the straight-arm lateral hold first if either shoulder talks. That's the designed exit.
Legs clean it, legs squat it, legs start the press. If the arm is working, go lighter.
Missing this day entirely does not make the week incomplete.
